messages:
maria: Hey team, I'm prepping a docs PR to add a minimal repro harness and a new SDK snippet showing graceful fallback from streaming -> non-streaming when we hit repeated 429s. PR draft: #4921

liam: SG. Paste the proposed snippet here? trying to keep it under 10 lines per language.

maria: sure, here's the Node example I'm thinking (stream -> fallback):

```js
const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) })
if (res.status === 200 && res.body) {
  // stream tokens to client
} else if (res.status === 429) {
  // fallback: exponential backoff + switch to non-stream mode
}
```

sam: runtime note: call out the `Retry-After` header and recommend randomized jitter on top of exponential backoff. Also add a sentence about trimming the context window before retrying if 409 / context-exceeded errors show up.

jen: QA can validate. I can spin the synthetic 429 generator if you add the curl steps.

maria: Added a tiny simulate command:

```bash
# simulate rate limit from dev-sim proxy
curl -X POST \"https://dev-sim.redwood.internal/simulate?code=429&rate=5\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"path":"/v1/generate","method":"POST"}'
```

liam: nice. pls also include an 'expected behavior' bullet list and a short troubleshooting checklist: token counting, partial-stream resume, mapping (429 -> retry/backoff, 408 -> client timeout -> increase socket timeout), plus links to err-ref pages.

maria: done in the draft. I added concise bullets and a small \"when to escalate to eng-runtime\" section.

docs-bot: PR created by maria: #4921 — reviewers requested: @liam @sam :eyes:

liam: I'll review tonight. If we can get the snippet ported to Python quickly, we can land both in one PR.

maria: I'll add Python snippet tomorrow morning and ping @jen for QA run when ready.

jen: ack, schedule looks good. I'll run the sim and post results as a follow-up thread.

sam: one more request — include a short note about Dedicated/Private differences: Dedicated may surface 429s differently (pool saturation) and Private may need operator-side rate-limiting rules. Keep it a single paragraph.

maria: added that too. PR is in good shape for a lightweight merge after liam review.

liam: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone.
